subject: Temporary credential escrow & portal upload plan
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@starlift-analytics.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Portal upload window + temp credentials (Starlift)

Hi Chloe,

We're starting the OneTrust profile upload for Redwood's vendor record and have a couple of nitty-gritty asks before we move files into the evidence bucket. Our security team can accept either: a) a short-lived presigned S3 upload URL with 48-72 hour TTL, or b) temporary IAM creds scoped to a single S3 prefix with a 7-day expiry. For audit reasons we need a written retention/escrow plan for those credentials — how Redwood prefers to hand off and rotate temporary credentials when we do the initial proof possession upload.

Can you confirm which option works, and who on your side will own the presign flow and audit trail? Also, we'll need the CAIQ mapping sheet for the items we're uploading so we can reference them in the portal.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Nguyen
Security Programs Manager
Starlift Analytics

Attachment: oneTrust-upload-guidance.pdf (reference only, we won't reattach)
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@starlift-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portal upload window + temp credentials (Starlift)

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we can support both flows; preference is a presigned-upload window for the initial evidence push (simpler auditing), then scoped temporary creds for incremental updates if you need programmatic sync.

Proposed plan:
- We generate presigned PUT URLs for the S3 prefix starlift-evidence/redwood-uploads/, TTL=72h.
- We publish a signed manifest + CAIQ mapping sheet inside the presigned bundle.
- After successful upload, Redwood will commit an audit entry and rotate any temporary access students (if used).

Ben, can you draft the presign flow & required metadata (headers, content-type expectations) and share the policy we intend to apply? Karthik, please confirm the portal role we'll ask Starlift to use (OneTrust vendor contact vs. read-only observer) so we map permissions correctly.

Claire — can you confirm whether OneTrust requires evidence links in a specific field (e.g., "Supporting Evidence URL") vs. a file attachment? That will affect whether we hand you URLs or ask you to download and attach.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Signature: Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portal upload window + temp credentials (Starlift)

Team — draft presign flow attached and a minimal temp-creds policy. Highlights:
- presign-flow.md: we will issue a batch of presigned PUT URLs tied to a manifest.json that lists expected filenames + SHA256. URLs expire 72h.
- temp-creds-policy.json: if Starlift needs automated sync, creds will be constrained to s3:PutObject and s3:ListBucket for prefix starlift-evidence/redwood-uploads/, and a short expiry (max 7d). No console access, no ability to modify buckets.

Audit/escrow note: we propose keeping a hashed copy of the manifest + a retention record (timestamp + issuer + expiry) in our internal evidence-audit bucket for 90 days; the actual presigned URLs are ephemeral and not stored. If customer requests credential escrow (customer-held backup of the policy), we can provide a signed policy stub but we cannot hand over active keys.

Attachments: presign-flow.md, temp-creds-policy.json

-ben
Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@starlift-analytics.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: claire.nguyen@starlift-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 07:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portal upload window + temp credentials (Starlift)

Thanks — that split approach sounds workable. A few clarifying Qs from our auditors:
1) When you say "hashed copy of the manifest" — will that include a signed timestamp (RFC3339) and Redwood's key id so our auditors can verify provenance?
2) For OneTrust uploads, we prefer direct file attachments in the vendor record (they won't accept external URLs for proof-of-possession fields). That means we'll either attach the files directly in the portal or attach a zip generated from the presigned uploads. Can your team produce the zip on completion and provide a checksum?

We're OK with presigned uploads + a post-upload zip/checksum, but we'll need the signed manifest and retention entry for our audit package.

Tim
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Starlift Analytics
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@starlift-analytics.com>, Timothy Barnes <tbarnes@starlift-analytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portal upload window + temp credentials (Starlift)

Great — thanks for the specifics, Tim. Finalized actions and timeline:
- Today (Nov 8): Ben will generate the presigned URL batch and the manifest; we will share a signed manifest (with RFC3339 timestamp and key-id) to Claire and Tim by EOD.
- Nov 9: Starlift performs upload into presigned prefix (72h window).
- Nov 10: Redwood will generate a zip of uploaded objects + SHA256 checksum and attach the zip to the OneTrust vendor record on your behalf. We will also record the retention row in our evidence-audit bucket (90-day retention).
- Post-upload: If Starlift needs an automated sync, we'll issue scoped temp creds for a 3-day window (requested separately).

Please confirm acceptance so we can trigger the presign batch. I'm linking the DocuSign for a short MAA (mutual access agreement) if you want the credential escrow language formalized. If you prefer, we can accept the audit package as an email acknowledgement instead.

Action: Claire — reply "ACK" to confirm and we'll start the presign run.

Thanks,
Chloe
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
